title: Atomic-Scale Three-Dimensional Phase Inhomogeneity and Interfacial Relaxation of Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2
content: Fluorite-structured HfO2/ZrO2 thin film is a promising candidate for next-generation scaled energy-efficient electronic devices due to its robust ferroelectricity down to unit-cell thickness and excellent silicon compatibility [1]. However, the thin film always has various polymorphs, and the desirable (anti)polar orthorhombic (O) phase are always coupled with the undesired nonpolar monoclinic (M) and tetragonal (T) phases [2]. The 3D phase inhomogeneity and transition can affect the ferroelectric degradation and the polarization recovery during electrical cycling and plays an important role on ferroelectric phase stabilization. Therefore, resolving the three-dimensional (3D) phase distribution in these films is essential to understand how phase inhomogeneity affect ferroelectric phase stability and to guide the development of stable and efficient fluorite oxide ferroelectric devices.
